#Question 1

age <- c(15, 28, 32, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 12, 42, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 8)

#Question 1a. How many data points?

length(age)
#34 data points

#Question 1b

1/age
#The reciprocal of age is:
#[1] 0.06666667 0.03571429 0.03125000 0.02777778 0.03703704 0.05555556 0.01923077 0.02564103 0.02380952
#[10] 0.03448276 0.02857143 0.03225806 0.03703704 0.04545455 0.02702703 0.02941176 0.05263158 0.05000000
#[19] 0.01754386 0.02040816 0.02000000 0.02702703 0.02173913 0.04000000 0.05882353 0.08333333 0.02380952
#[28] 0.01886792 0.02439024 0.01960784 0.02857143 0.04166667 0.03030303 0.12500000

#Question 1c

new_age <- c(age, 0, age)
length(new_age)
#new_age is a new vector that contains all of age, then a single 0, then all of age again. Its length is 34 + 1 + 34 = 69. The original age vector is unchanged.

#Question 1d

min(age)
max(age)
#The minimum is 8 and the maximum is 57.

#Question 2

rep(c("A","B"), each = 2)
rep(c("A","B"), times = 2)
#each repeats every element individually before moving to the next one. So “A” is repeated 2 times, then “B” is repeated 2 times.
#times repeats the whole vector from start to finish. So the full sequence “A”, “B” is copied 2 times.
